pages.title: Wōkerer
pages.hint: A byname heard on the quay
pages.brief: The usurer: a man who lends silver and takes back more. It is what your creditor is called on the quay.
pages.game: Your creditor is called the Wōkerer, though not to his face. You owe him the price of your boat by the day he named. If the silver is short on that day he takes her back, with whatever lies in her.
pages.known:
From wōker, usury: silver grown from silver. The word is in Old English as wōcor and in Old High German as wuohhar, and lives on as Dutch woeker and German Wucher; the Old Frisian form is the one to be expected and has not been checked against a dictionary (?).
The Church forbade usury to its clergy at Nicaea in 325, and the Admonitio generalis of 789 forbade it to everyone in the Frankish realm: a man who lent at interest was known for it, and not kindly.
